title: Part Time Administrator
description:
Are you an organised, approachable, and customer-focused Administrator looking to make a real difference in Scarborough? Would you like to work for an organisation known for delivering high-quality client support and trusted by the community it serves? Are you looking to join a supportive, client-focused organisation where teamwork and service excellence are at the core?

If so, this could be the perfect opportunity for you. We are recruiting for a part-time Administrator (21.25 hours per week) on a 9-month fixed-term contract to provide maternity cover. This varied role offers the chance to become part of a friendly and supportive team, providing excellent service to clients and playing a key role in the smooth running of the organisation.

What the Administrator job involves

As an Administrator, you will be the first point of contact for clients, ensuring they receive a friendly, efficient, and professional service. Your responsibilities will include:
- Handling client enquiries with care, offering guidance and directing them to the right services both over the phone and via email.
- Managing and booking appointments efficiently using the in-house CRM system.
- Processing and distributing correspondence, both electronically and by mail.
- Supporting the wider team with administrative duties including data entry, filing, scanning and record maintenance.
- Providing accurate information to clients and colleagues to ensure smooth communication across departments.
- Answering the telephone and taking accurate messages to send to colleagues at all levels within the organisation.
- Supporting the reception team by contributing to a welcoming and professional environment, both in person and over the phone.

Skills required
- Previous experience in an administration, coordination or office-based customer service role.
- Strong IT and data entry skills with knowledge of Microsoft Office packages.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.
- A flexible, conscientious and team-oriented approach.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
- A proactive attitude and willingness to learn.

Other information
- Part-time 21.25 hours per week
- 9-month fixed-term maternity cover contract
- Enhanced pension
- Car parking available
- 22 days' holiday plus bank holidays (pro rata)
- Access to a discount scheme across a number of platforms and retailers
- Overtime pay available

This vacancy is being advertised through KD Recruitment Limited who are operating as an Employment Agency.

Due to the volume of applications we receive, if you have not heard from us within two weeks, please assume you have not been shortlisted for this particular role.

KD Recruitment Limited is committed to a policy of equal opportunities in relation to job applications and is also committed to protecting your personal data. If you would like to read our Privacy Policy, please visit our website at (url removed), where you will find all the information you need to know about how we will use and process your personal data.

You can also follow us on Facebook, Instagram, X and LinkedIn for up-to-date vacancies and other helpful information.

title: Recruitment Coordinator
description:
Recruitment Coordinator - Gi Group

Location: Scarborough (on-site)

Contract: Full-time, permanent

Hours: Thursday - Monday

Salary: 27,450 plus bonus and Award Winning benefits

As a Recruitment Coordinator, you will support the day-to-day delivery of recruitment and workforce solutions for client accounts. Working closely with clients, candidates and internal teams, you'll coordinate recruitment activity, keep information up to date and help ensure service requirements are met efficiently and professionally.

Key responsibilities
- Support the day-to-day coordination of client accounts and recruitment activity.
- Receive and clarify client requirements, vacancies and staffing priorities, sharing information with the relevant teams.
- Coordinate candidate sourcing, interviews, feedback and availability with recruiters, clients and candidates.
- Help manage candidate bookings, placements, onboarding and other account administration in line with agreed processes.
- Respond to client and candidate queries promptly, escalating issues where appropriate.
- Maintain accurate records of vacancies, candidates, placements and account activity in the applicant tracking system (ATS) and other databases.
- Monitor recruitment progress, service requirements and deadlines, providing updates to clients and internal stakeholders.
- Prepare reports and support account reviews, compliance checks and other administrative tasks as required.
- Build positive working relationships with clients, candidates and colleagues, contributing to a consistent, high-quality service.

About you
- Experience in account coordination, recruitment administration, customer service or a similar role is desirable.
- Strong organisation and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines.
- Clear and professional communication skills, with a helpful and responsive approach.
- Excellent attention to detail when handling candidate, client and placement information.
- Confident building relationships and working collaboratively with a range of stakeholders.
- Comfortable using Microsoft Office and willing to learn recruitment systems, including ATS and client databases.
- Proactive and adaptable, with a solution-focused approach in a fast-paced environment.
- A commitment to providing a professional and inclusive experience for clients and candidates.

What we offer
- Structured training and ongoing development opportunities.
- A supportive, collaborative team environment.
- Opportunities to develop your account management and recruitment coordination skills.

Additional information
- We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds.
- Applicants must have the right to work in the UK.

Should you require any support or assistance, please contact your local Gi Group office.

Gi Group Holdings Recruitment Limited are proud founding members of Menopause in business, pledge members for Neurodiversity in business, Disability committed members, Gold status pledge members for the Armed Forces Covenant, and Bronze trail blazers for Racial Equality matters.

We are committed to protecting the privacy of all our candidates and clients. If you choose to apply, your information will be processed in accordance with the Gi Group Privacy Statement. To view a copy and to help you understand how we collect, use and process your personal data please visit the Privacy page on our Gi Group website.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: We are seeking a compassionate and proactive Medical Receptionist to join our busy GP practice team. This is a key front-line role, supporting patients to access the right care, at the right time, from the right service. You will help patients navigate primary care services, community resources and external agencies, ensuring they receive appropriate, timely and coordinated support. Working closely with GPs, nurses, and the wider multidisciplinary team, you will act as a central point of contact for patients, helping to manage enquiries, signpost effectively, and improve overall patient experience. The role requires excellent communication skills, sound judgement, strong organisational ability, and a calm, professional approach in a fast-paced environment. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who is passionate about patient-centred care and wants to make a genuine difference within their local community. Act as the first point of contact for patient enquiries, gathering relevant information sensitively and accurately. Signpost patients to appropriate clinicians, services or community support in line with practice protocols. Support care coordination for patients with long-term conditions and complex needs. Process and manage appointment requests in line with triage guidance. Liaise with the wider multidisciplinary team to ensure seamless patient journeys. Maintain accurate clinical records and update patient information on the clinical system. Contribute to improving access, patient flow and overall patient experience. You will act as a first point of contact for patients and external agencies, responding to enquiries professionally and sensitively, whether in person, by telephone or electronically. You will gather relevant information, care navigate in line with practice protocols, and ensure patients are directed to the most appropriate clinician or service. You will also support home visit requests and liaise with community and secondary care providers where required. You will manage appointment systems effectively, including booking, amending and cancelling appointments, processing recalls and supporting demand management processes. This includes recording accurate information on the clinical system, supporting long-term condition monitoring and ensuring patients receive timely follow-up. The role also includes general administrative duties such as processing incoming and outgoing correspondence, scanning and coding documents, maintaining accurate patient records, and providing clerical support to the wider team. You will contribute to maintaining smooth day-to-day operations within the practice and undertake mandatory training as required.
